issue.title: copyChipSerialize picks a bob-copy fence marker that an indented ``` body line closes early

task_type_fields.impact: Mod+Shift+Y (Make or edit chip) can write a bob-copy fence whose copied payload silently loses everything after an indented ``` line. The note text is not lost, but the chip copies the wrong bytes. It is rare: the text must contain an indented triple-backtick line.
task_type_fields.repro:
In bob-plugins (master ee941a1+):

```bash
node -e 'const { helpers } = require("./scripts/copy-chips-test-helpers.cjs");
console.log(JSON.stringify(helpers.copyChipSerialize({ label: null, text: "a\n  ```\nb" })));'
```

Output: `{"ok":true,"form":"block","markdown":"```bob-copy\na\n  ```\nb\n```"}`. The body line "  ```" (indented up to 3 spaces) is a valid CommonMark closer, so the fence closes early and the payload truncates to "a".

Root cause: copyChipSerialize in `plugins/bob-chips/src/020-grammar.js` counts backtick runs only at column 0 when choosing the fence marker. runChipSerialize already avoids this with its closer-aware marker choice (bob-cli-nu.3). Fix: count runs after leading whitespace (as runChipSerialize does) and update the copy vectors deliberately. scripts/test-command-chips-grammar.cjs pins COPY_VECTORS_SHA256, so re-pin it in the same change. This is an intentional copy-chip behavior change, so record it in docs/bob-chips.md.

issue.creation_reason: Proposed by bob-cli-nu.3 (note #1) and triaged by the bob-cli-nu land agent; copy chips were kept byte-stable during the command-chip epic (C11), so this pre-existing serializer defect was left for its own change.
